commands.review_summary:
Adds a review-content digest/cache gate that carries forward completed reports for unchanged automatic re-reviews, persists cache metadata, and adds focused scheduler/digest tests.

Reproducibility: not applicable. as a performance PR rather than a bug report. The PR body provides live-output proof and the added tests exercise the skip-versus-spawn decisions.

target.title: perf(review): reuse prior verdict when reviewable content is unchanged
target.body:
## Problem

`shouldReviewItem` (src/scheduler-policy.ts) gates the review-lane model call on time cadence plus the review-policy hash only. `reviewCommand`'s per-item loop then calls `runCodex` unconditionally for every selected item. Idle PRs are re-reviewed daily and idle issues weekly, and any activity drops the cadence to hourly. With openclaw/openclaw currently at ~3,480 open PRs and ~3,615 open issues, a large share of daily model calls re-derive a byte-identical verdict from byte-identical input. Each is a cold-start `codex exec` at high reasoning effort with a 10-30 minute timeout that also holds one of the 128 worker slots.

The content fingerprint needed to detect "unchanged" already exists (`itemSnapshotHash`, persisted as `item_snapshot_hash`) but is computed after the model runs and only used downstream, so it never gates the model.

## Change

- `itemContentDigest(item, context)` (src/clawsweeper.ts) hashes the review-relevant, bot-immune, timestamp-free surface: `kind`, `context.sourceRevision` (title, body, filtered labels, non-bot conversation comments), and for PRs the head sha, base sha, `pullFiles` diff, and inline review comments (author, association, body; bot-authored comments and timestamps stripped). It excludes `updatedAt`, the live main sha, and ClawSweeper's own comments.
- `reviewContentCacheHit(...)` and `REVIEW_CACHE_MAX_AGE_DAYS = 14` (src/scheduler-policy.ts) return true only when the prior review is complete, the policy matches, the digest matches, it is not an explicit or maintainer re-review, and the last full review is under 14 days old. Two optional fields were added to `SchedulerExistingReview`.
- `markdownFor` persists `review_content_digest` and `last_full_review_at`; `existingReview` and `buildExistingReviewIndex` read them back into `ExistingReview`.
- In the review loop, on an automatic run, the prior report is looked up and, on a cache hit, carried forward with only liveness fields refreshed (`reviewed_at`, `item_updated_at`, `item_snapshot_hash`, `main_sha`, `pull_head_sha`) while the model call is skipped and a `cache_hits` counter and log line are emitted. The verdict, `last_full_review_at`, and comment metadata are preserved.

## Why it is safe

Identical review input yields an identical verdict, so the skip cannot change an outcome. `item_snapshot_hash` and the apply lane's `skipped_changed_since_review` protection are unchanged: the carry-forward writes the current snapshot hash and live `item_updated_at`, exactly as a real review would. First-ever reviews, failed or incomplete priors, policy bumps, any real content change, explicit re-review, maintainer prompts, and the 14-day ceiling all fall through to a full review. Pre-rollout reports lack the digest field and are re-reviewed once, self-migrating.

## Before/after behavior proof

Reproducing the loop guard (`if (reviewContentCacheHit) continue; else runCodex`) with the real compiled gate and a fake `codex` on `PATH` that counts real subprocess spawns, over four identical-cadence re-reviews (first-ever, unchanged, changed diff, new maintainer review comment):

```
base (no content gate)  spawns=4 over [full, unchanged, changed, new-review-comment]
patched (content skip)  spawns=3 decisions=[spawn, skip, spawn, spawn]
```

The unchanged re-review skips the model; a first-ever review, a real diff change, and a new maintainer review comment all still run it.

## Target-branch state and close verdicts

A `close` verdict can depend on target-branch code (for example `implemented_on_main`), which is not in the content digest because the live main sha advances on every merge and would collapse the cache. To keep close decisions safe, a cache hit for a `close` verdict additionally requires the stored `main_sha` to equal the current one: if main moved since the review that produced the close, the item gets a full re-review before any close. So a close is never carried forward across target-branch state it was not verified against. `keep_open` verdicts cache on content alone; a stale keep-open only delays a close (never causes a wrongful one) and is bounded by the 14-day ceiling.

## Trade-offs

- Base-branch drift that changes the effective PR diff busts the cache via the head sha, base sha, and `pullFiles`.
- Between full reviews, a `keep_open` issue whose fix lands on main (with no issue-side activity) can stay open up to `REVIEW_CACHE_MAX_AGE_DAYS` (14) before the next full review proposes the close. This is the non-destructive direction and is bounded by the ceiling and by any content change.

## Tests

`test/review-content-cache.test.ts` (15 cases): digest stability across bot-only context churn; digest busts on body, diff-patch, head-sha, and base-sha changes; issue vs PR field isolation; and the gate returning true only when unchanged, fresh, complete, and policy-matched, and false on policy bump, past the 14-day ceiling, explicit re-review, maintainer request, prior-failed, first-ever, and pre-digest reports.
